Sign-In Screen

The yard is the screen. No card, no panel — the logo sits on the artwork and the three ways in sit under it, with a scrim carrying them over the busiest part of the picture. Everything below is drawn at the real canvas proportions, so what you see is what the build lays out.

What sits where

Positions in canvas units, the numbers the C# actually uses. The screen is 800 × 1730 — reference width 800, match-width, at a 2.16 aspect.

ElementUnitsWhy
Logo 470 sq
top 150		 Square art, so a square rect. High enough that the scene reads under it.
Subtitle top 632 Twelve units under the logo — one block, not two.
Buttons 520 × 104
gap 26		 65% of the width. Thumb-sized, and wide enough that the badge doesn't crowd the label.
Button column 762 – 1162 Starts clear of the subtitle, ends well above the small print.
Icon badge 62
inset 22		 Facebook a filled disc; the other two a ring.
Legal bottom 40 Two real links, not a rich-text field, so the taps are actual rects.

This caught a bug. Laying it out in real units showed the button column sitting at 575–975, which runs straight through the subtitle at 632–732 — the text would have rendered on top of the Facebook button. The column moves down to 762. The screen above uses the corrected number.

Labels stay centred on the button, not in the space left beside the badge. Centring them in the remainder staggers the three labels against each other; centring on the button keeps them in a line down the column, which is what you read.

Facebook keeps its own blue. It's the one control here that is somebody else's brand, and people find it by colour before they read it. The other two take the game's own palette.

Artwork is lobby-rum.png and Pose-logo.png from the project, downscaled and embedded. Type is Baloo 2 and Nunito — the pair DESIGN_SYSTEM.md §3 specifies, loaded for real here rather than substituted. Buttons and the email form are live: press them.
